record.context_brief: Divergent trajectories in generalized Syracuse maps
record.original_question: Let a and b be odd integers with a > −b and a + b = 2^ν₀, and let T(n)=n/2 for even n and T(n)=(a n+b)/2 for odd n. Let G(∞) be the set of positive starting values n for which T^k(n) tends to infinity. Which conditions on a and b make G(∞) empty, and which conditions make G(∞) nonempty? Equivalently, for which such maps does every trajectory eventually enter a finite cycle rather than diverge?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a$ and $b$ be odd integers satisfying $a > -b$ and $a + b = 2^{\nu_0}$ for some positive integer $\nu_0$. Define the map $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ by
$$T(n) = \begin{cases} n/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is even},\\ (an+b)/2 & \text{if } n \text{ is odd}. \end{cases}$$
For each starting value $n \in \mathbb{N}$, consider the trajectory $\{T^{(k)}(n)\}_{k \geq 0}$ obtained by iterating $T$. Define
$$G(\infty) = \{\, n \in \mathbb{N} : \lim_{k \to \infty} T^{(k)}(n) = \infty \,\}.$$
Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the pair $(a,b)$ (subject to the standing assumptions above) under which $G(\infty)$ is empty, and conditions under which $G(\infty)$ is nonempty. Equivalently, characterize those parameters $(a,b)$ for which every positive integer trajectory of $T$ eventually enters a finite cycle, as opposed to diverging to infinity.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a generalization of the Collatz (Syracuse) conjecture. Even the classical case $a=3$, $b=1$ remains famously open (Lagarias, Tao 2019 partial result on almost-bounded trajectories). No general characterization of $(a,b)$ producing only bounded trajectories is known, and the question is widely regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: The Collatz conjecture, Littlewood-Offord, and powers of 2 and 3
status_evidence.snippet: Tao proves almost all Collatz orbits attain almost bounded values; the full Collatz conjecture remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Even the classical Syracuse case (a=3,b=1) is unresolved, indicating the generalized question on divergent trajectories is also open.
